newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end volatile day higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end volatile day higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Friday following volatile trade, with the Hang Seng Index recovering some of Thursday's sharp losses after finding support at the 13,800 level in morning trade, brokers said.

The blue chip barometer ended up 188.21 points, or 1.35 percent, at 14,112.55. The Hang Seng soared to a day's high of 14,145 in early trade, crashed to 13,795 on index futures related selling in mid-morning, and then clambered up again.
"Market sentiment improved in the afternoon with mainland investors seen buying red-chips," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
But brokers were uncertain whether or not the latest market correction was completed. The Hang Seng had fallen about 907 points in five consecutive losing sessions.
"It's a technical rebound today but whether the market has stablised is still unable to be confirmed yet," said Josephine Hui, head of research at Cheerful Research.
"The rebound is not very strong considering yesterday's 497 point loss and the sharp gains in overseas markets," Hui said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average set its fifth straight record close overnight at 7,711.47, up 135.64 points on the day.
Analysts said the Wall Street rally was fuelled by optimism that the Federal Reserve probably would not lift interest rates in July following positive economic data released recently.
Hong Kong's blue chips were mixed while red chips were generally firmer after a day of volatile trading.
HSBC rose HK$3.00 to HK$230.00 and Hongkong Telecom surged HK$0.65 to HK$16.35 but Sun Hung Kai Properties was down HK$0.25 to HK$85.75.
Property stocks were clounded by concerns about possible new government measures aimed at cooling property speculation, brokers said.
But worries over China's measures to calm speculation in mainland stock markets seemed to have eased following Thursday's loss cutting sales, they said.
Following heavy sell offs of China-related red chips in recent days, any money that mainland investors may still have to pull out of the market was likely to be limited, Hui said.
CITIC Pacific surged HK$2.40 to HK$45.40, Shaunghai Industrial added HK$1.40 to HK$41.20 and China Merchant Hai Hong jumped HK$2.25 to HK$15.25.
Turnover shrank to HK$15.40 billion from Thursday's HK$17.43 billion.
